findings.title: Deleting the cache does not refresh the connected-calendars query
findings.body:
The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only toasts and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation does this in `onSettled` (line 61-64), so the two actions behave differently.

The settings page happens to pass an `onChanged` that invalidates the query (`apps/web/components/apps/CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88`). The event-type Advanced tab does not pass `onChanged` (`packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372`). Only the connected-calendars query reads `cacheUpdatedAt`, and `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` sets `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`.

So on the Advanced tab the toast says the cache was deleted, but "Last updated: …" keeps its old value and "Delete cached data" stays available. The fix is to invalidate `connectedCalendars` inside the dropdown's `deleteCacheMutation`, as the disconnect mutation does.

findings.title: Handler bypasses the repository, throws a plain Error, and the input schema is inline
findings.body: The handler calls `prisma.credential.findFirst` and `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly. `CalendarCacheRepository` already exists in this PR and is used by the sibling `connectedCalendars` handler. The not-found case throws `new Error(...)`, which tRPC turns into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. The sibling `setDestinationCalendar.handler.ts` throws `TRPCError`, so use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` here. The input schema is declared inline in `_router.tsx:29` with a new `zod` import, while the other procedures in this router use `*.schema.ts` files. Consider a `deleteCache.schema.ts` and a repository method such as `deleteManyByCredential`; the interface and mock already have a method with that name, so check whether it can be reused.

findings.title: Why bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt with an empty updateMany?
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})` relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` behaviour for an empty `data` object. Nothing in this PR reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The new `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` fields in `UserWithCalendars` and `user.ts` are selected but never used, and the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This adds an extra write on every Google webhook and every unwatch. It also makes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` stop reflecting real changes to the row. The call also sits outside any try/catch, so if the write fails the webhook returns an error after the cache was already refreshed. Is there a consumer for this value? If not, drop the call along with the unused selected fields and type additions.

findings.title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded "en-US" locale
findings.body: `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's locale, even though the label is translated through `t()`. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) or the app's date helpers. Also, `cache_status` and the cache strings were added only to the `en` locale file, which is the usual process for this repo, so that part is fine.

findings.title: Cache deletion is offered where connection changes are meant to be disabled
findings.body: `hasCache` ignores `disableConnectionModification`. On the event-type Advanced tab, which passes `disableConnectionModification={true}` (`EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375`), the dropdown now appears with "Delete cached data". The `deleteCache` mutation deletes the cache for the whole credential, so it affects every event type and the user-level setting. Decide whether this action should be gated by `disableConnectionModification` too. Also note the second `actions` block (error alert) previously did not check `disableConnectionModification` and now does. That is a behaviour change on the settings page.

findings.title: Stale auto-generated warning contradicts the SQL below it
findings.body: The header says the column was added "without a default value" and "is not possible if the table is not empty". Line 9 adds `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is false. Existing rows all get the migration time as `updatedAt`, which the UI then shows as "Last updated" even though the data may be older. Remove the warning and note this in the comment.

findings.title: Unrelated dev script that is macOS-only and cwd-dependent
findings.body: This script and the `dev:cron` change to `npx tsx` (`apps/web/package.json:11`) are unrelated to the cache-status feature. `sed -i ''` (line 68) works only with BSD sed, so it breaks on Linux. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves against the current directory, not the script's location, so it only works if run from a subdirectory of the repo. `cleanup` runs `exit 0` on the failure paths (lines 49 and 58), so callers see success when no URL was obtained. `tsx` is not a declared dependency (`ts-node` is), so `npx tsx` fetches an unpinned package at run time. Consider splitting these changes out or fixing them.

contracts.action: User clicks "Delete cached data" and confirms
contracts.equivalent_path: Disconnect mutation in the same file (line 53-65) and DisconnectIntegration.tsx, which invalidates connectedCalendars and integrations in onSettled
contracts.before_after: The new path deletes the cache and calls only the optional onSuccess prop. The disconnect path also invalidates queries itself. The settings page's onChanged invalidates connectedCalendars, but the Advanced tab passes no onChanged.
contracts.visible_effect: Success toast. "Last updated" and the delete option remain on the Advanced tab until the query refetches.
contracts.failure_mode: On rejection the mutation shows an error toast and the dialog is already closed. The cache is left intact and nothing is lost.

contracts.action: deleteCache handler destructively deletes all CalendarCache rows for a credential
contracts.equivalent_path: CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential (interface and mock exist) and the cache repopulation done by the Google webhook
contracts.before_after: Before the delete, the handler re-queries the credential by id and ownership (userId = ctx.user.id). The delete is scoped to `credentialId`, and the ownership check happens in the same request immediately before it. Cache rows are only a cache; they are repopulated by the next webhook (webhook.ts:46) or an availability fetch.
contracts.visible_effect: All cache entries for that credential are removed, including entries for other event-type scopes. The next availability lookup falls back to the live Google API call.
contracts.failure_mode: Negative in-memory delegation credential ids are not found, so the handler throws a plain Error. The user sees the generic error toast. Team-owned credentials are rejected the same way. A DB error rejects the mutation and nothing is deleted.

contracts.action: connectedCalendars handler adds a cache status query
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing flow returns connectedCalendars straight from getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb
contracts.before_after: A groupBy on CalendarCache by credentialId is added after the existing call. It uses the real CalendarCacheRepository directly, not the mock selected when calendar-cache is disabled.
contracts.visible_effect: Each connected calendar gets cacheUpdatedAt (the max updatedAt, or null).
contracts.failure_mode: If the groupBy throws, the whole connectedCalendars query fails, not just the cache status. Delegation credentials with negative ids simply yield no rows.

contracts.action: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now updates all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential
contracts.equivalent_path: upsertCachedAvailability sets CalendarCache.updatedAt via @updatedAt on the upsert
contracts.before_after: After the cache upserts, an updateMany with empty data runs for the credential. Nothing in the repository reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.
contracts.failure_mode: If it throws, the webhook handler fails after the cache has already been written. Whether Prisma actually bumps updatedAt for empty data is not established.
contracts.open_question: Is there a consumer of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, and does Prisma updateMany with {} update the @updatedAt column?

summary:
The cache-status dropdown is mostly sound: the ownership check in `deleteCache` is correct, and the groupBy query and migration default are fine. The one defect I'd fix is that deleting the cache doesn't invalidate the connected-calendars query. On the event-type Advanced tab, which passes no `onChanged`, the toast says the cache was deleted but "Last updated" and the delete option stay on screen.

Smaller points:
- `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is touched on every refresh, but nothing reads it, and I couldn't confirm Prisma updates `@updatedAt` for empty `data`.
- The handler bypasses the repository and throws a plain `Error`.
- The timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `en-US` locale.
- Cache deletion is offered where `disableConnectionModification` is true.
- The migration's header comment contradicts its SQL.
- `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` is macOS-only and unrelated to this feature.

I only read the code; nothing was built or run, and there are no tests for the new handler or repository method."
